title: House passes bill penalizing piracy sites, counterfeit sellers up to P1 million
summary: A bill increasing penalties on piracy sites and other counterfeit art sellers to P1 million has been approved on third and final reading in the House of Representatives.

blocks.text: A bill increasing penalties on piracy sites and other counterfeit art sellers to P1 million has been approved on third and final reading in the House of Representatives.
This developed after House Bill 11616 got 234 yes votes during the House’s plenary session on Wednesday.

The bill allows copyright owners and rights holders such as Filipino writers, musicians, filmmakers and business owners to ask the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPOPHL) to block access to websites or other online locations whose primary purpose or effect is to infringe copyright or facilitate infringement.

Blocking would require due notice and hearing, while notification of a complaint to the site operator could be dispensed with only under specified conditions involving unsuccessful reasonable efforts to identify, locate or notify that operator.

Once a petition for blocking is found meritorious, internet service providers would then have to comply with a disabling order within 48 hours of its issuance by applying effective technical measures to prevent access to the identified location.

An existing disabling order would also cover additional online locations associated with the infringing operation through their name, branding or operator, addressing attempts to evade blocking by moving to another address.
As for the fees, the bill pegged the administrative fines to P100,000 to P1 million or way above the existing P5,000 to P150,000.
The measure also includes infringing electronic and digital content in its definition of pirated goods, recognizing that unauthorized reproduction and distribution also occur online.
Trademark protection could extend beyond visible signs, provided a sign is capable of distinguishing one enterprise’s goods or services from another’s.
A single complaint could cover multiple infringing online locations, allowing rights holders to pursue related sites together when the required information is supplied.

The bill also grants IPOPHL authority to gather intelligence, investigate suspected violations, visit establishments during reasonable hours and recommend that the appropriate authorities cancel business permits or licenses.
